text: 🔥🇲🇽 "He is a sellout and a traitor." Sheinbaum on those who take Mexico's internal fights to a foreign government. Dragging domestic disputes before Washington, she says, is a betrayal of the country. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on Alito Moreno's US lobbying The PRI leader gives more interviews abroad than at home and hires foreign consultants over Mexican experts. She asked the INE to check whether it is legal.

🇲🇽⚖️ "They must be honest people, with no record of any link to crime or any act of corruption." Sheinbaum's bar for Morena's 2027 candidates as the party opens nominations in Campeche, Colima and Aguascalientes. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on 2027 candidacies Electoral law lets the party ask the INE to vet aspirants for organized-crime ties. Candidates are chosen by poll, not by the leadership.

🇲🇽🏭 Record foreign investment: $34.968 billion in the first half of 2026 — an all-time high. "Several pieces of good economic news," Sheinbaum said, and listed the numbers. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the economy FDI up 2.1% year-on-year, GDP +1.4% in Q2 (best since 2022), a strong peso, no inflation, 60 million people employed. The capital flight the opposition predicted never came.

🔥🇲🇽 "Salinas did not win the presidency." Sheinbaum on Carlos Salinas, who took power in the fraud-stained 1988 election — the "caída del sistema." For millions of Mexicans, he never legitimately won. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the 1988 election That sexenio bailed out banks and companies while abandoning the people — the neoliberal template the 4T says it reversed.

🇲🇽🌎 A face-to-face with Trump? "When we reach an agreement, then we could meet." Asked about a bilateral with Trump on security, migration and tariffs, Sheinbaum set the condition: an agreement first. No rush for the photo op. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on a bilateral with Trump She has held 21 phone calls with Trump. Still no formal bilateral scheduled — the talks move at Mexico's pace.

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico has to be present — but that does not mean we stop defending our principles of sovereignty, independence, non-interference and non-subordination." Trump is hosting the G20 in Miami this December. Sheinbaum confirmed the invitation and said Mexico will attend to represent itself — without surrendering its foreign-policy principles. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the G20 Miami summit 21 phone calls with Trump, no bilateral yet. Cooperation with Washington, not subordination to it.

🇲🇽📈 <u>ONE SECTOR CARRIED HALF OF MEXICO'S Q2 GROWTH</u>

Wholesale commerce surged 11.3% in Q2 and single-handedly delivered almost half of Mexico's growth — nearly 1 of the 2.1 percentage points the economy advanced, per El Financiero's Enrique Quintana citing INEGI. Strip it out and growth falls to about 1.2%. Five sectors — wholesale, construction, agriculture, mining and government — account for 84% of the annual gain, a rebound that's real but unusually concentrated.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>MEXICO CITY ADDS 800 FREE CLINICS TO ITS UNIVERSAL HEALTH SYSTEM</u>

Mexico City is folding 800 neighborhood clinics into a universal public health system — free consultations, labs, medicines, mental-health care and chronic-disease screening for everyone, regardless of job or income. It's one slice of a federal rollout of 12,750 clinics across 24 states. "We have a historic opportunity to produce health in the territories," said Mayor Clara Brugada.

🇲🇽🌹 <u>MORENA LINES UP ITS 2027 SLATE — AND WOMEN ARE LEADING IT</u>

Morena named Rosi Bayardo, ex-mayor of Manzanillo, as its Colima coordinator and likely 2027 gubernatorial candidate — one of several women, alongside Nora Ruvalcaba in Aguascalientes, the party is advancing for the next cycle. Bayardo, a psychologist who's organized the state since 2017, contrasted the 4T's Colima with the "financial crisis" the PRI-PAN administration left behind.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US AND CANADA SOUND ALARMS OVER MEXICALI — MEXICO SAYS SHOW THE EVIDENCE</u>

The US Consulate in Tijuana and Canada both issued security alerts over a vague "threat" in Mexicali, telling citizens to avoid public buildings. Mexico's Security Cabinet checked and pushed back: "there are no elements that confirm a specific or imminent risk." Patrols were reinforced anyway, but the pattern is familiar — foreign alarm bells over Mexican cities, no evidence attached.
